purpose: Versioned, evidence-backed mapping from registered components and their declared consumers to repository test targets for R/O/G pull-request validation.
claim_ceiling: This map selects repository validation only. It does not establish real-world causal effects, grant execution or publication authority, or replace required shared security, permission, evidence, review, or release checks.

targets.evidence: Existing incremental-planner, authority, and defensive-rejection tests plus negative router, exact-plan/receipt, deterministic component-bundle, rollback-selection, final-main-witness, and final-main-witness workflow-path coverage fixtures exercise component closure and fail-closed release evidence.
Existing current-state sync, surface compilation and state-change tests exercise the affected declared consumers.
Existing epistemic relationship, ESI human-surface, soft-governance authority, and durability tests exercise the declared G boundary consumers without granting truth or permission authority.
Existing federation contract, ownership, and adversarial tests exercise the declared executor and future-slot permission, interface, and evidence boundaries.

The existing Foundation test suite consumes formal-object records and schemas, while the canonical Lean Foundation proof command validates the formal proof consumer boundary. One execution covers both registered consumers.
Existing Foundation claim-governance and nonfunction-closure consumers validate L3 argument and claim relationships.
A focused test validates the existing historical rights-remediation register against its schema and reconciles its declared summary from the register entries without rewriting historical records.
These existing tests cover the registered no-L7 and system-map/front-door projection constraints.
These test modules are the existing registered consumers of Ignition Operating Method and its run-mode, capability, lifecycle, output and stranger-agent boundaries.
These existing publication and synchronization consumer tests cover L6/iteration publication constraints.
These existing consumers validate Foundation path classification and the propagation/era-resolution contracts affected by the L5 classification source.
Existing human-result and knowledge-experience validators and tests cover the registered human_knowledge_surfaces outputs and their derived consumers.

PR #259 candidate package tests: test_research_workflow.py covers the live CLI with OpenAlex and Crossref; test_pluggable_slot.py covers the independent offline/source-binding slot. The output receipts do not enter the canonical O human-knowledge surfaces.
The existing decision-integrity contract, gate, R2 reproduction and R3 evaluator consumer tests validate evidence binding and fail-closed semantic evaluation for the registered decision components.
Existing Q43 real-CLI, direct-predecessor, semantic positive, false-value, and evidence-laundering tests cover the contract, pilot, and validator paths.
Existing Q45 direct gate, R2 evidence-binding, and R3 semantic-evaluator tests cover the declared context protocol contract, pilot, and validator paths.

A uniquely named unittest target invokes the existing pytest regression and scenario modules so their real test cases execute through the Foundation router without namespace shadowing; the evidence remains repository-local and grants no production or scientific authority.

The registered ARR static gate and focused pytest suite exercise adapter-only boundaries, fixtures, schemas, and growth-ceiling controls; existing router tests preserve exact target and fail-closed routing behavior. The six synthetic R3 corpus modules cover inventory, semantic analysis, checkpoint/resume, privacy boundaries, aggregation, and acceptance without loading the private WAIC corpus or enabling PROMOTE/EVOLVE.
